# 04-final-validation: Build, smoke-test, and document follow-ups

Perform the full solution build after task 03 completes and confirm 0 build errors. Since Test Coverage was skipped, no automated regression suite exists — perform a basic manual/smoke check of core MVC flows (home, courses, students, instructors, departments, notifications) if feasible.

Document any deferred recommendations surfaced during the upgrade: the MSMQ replacement decision (if isolated rather than fully replaced), any binding-redirect entries that were kept rather than removed and why, and any System.Web Adapters limitations encountered.

**Done when**: The solution builds with 0 errors on `net10.0`, and deferred recommendations (MSMQ, binding redirects, adapter limitations) are documented for the user.

## Research findings (this task)

- **Project**: single project, `ContosoUniversity.csproj`, already SDK-style, `TargetFramework=net10.0` (confirmed in the csproj — 03.10 was the last per-controller migration and left the project fully converted).
- **03.10 (last controller task) already ran** `rm -rf obj bin && dotnet build` and reported 0 errors/0 warnings, and a repo-wide grep for `using System\.Web`, `HttpPostedFileBase`, `Server\.MapPath` returning zero matches in `.cs` files. This task re-verifies that independently rather than trusting it, per the workflow reminder about stale-cache false claims.
- **Binding redirects** (`tasks/03.01-tfm-packages-bindingredirects/binding-redirects.md`): all 12 assessment-flagged issues (6 `<dependentAssembly>` entries) were removed from `Web.config` as obsolete. A note in that doc explicitly flags **14 more `<dependentAssembly>` entries left in place** (`Microsoft.Web.Infrastructure`, `Antlr3.Runtime`, `System.Web.Optimization`, `WebGrease`, `System.Web.Helpers`, `System.Web.WebPages`, `System.Web.Mvc`, plus 7 `Microsoft.Extensions.*`/`netstandard` entries) because they weren't among the assessment's 12 flagged issues — out of scope for 03.01, deferred to a follow-up. Confirmed still present in `Web.config` by direct read. These are inert under `net10.0` (the CLR feature they rely on doesn't exist outside .NET Framework) but harmless; recommend documenting as a deferred cleanup rather than blocking this task on removing them (scenario strategy is "Document and Review Before Removing", not blanket-delete).
- **MSMQ** (`tasks/03.04-msmq-replacement/progress-details.md`): replaced `System.Messaging` with the drop-in `MSMQ.Messaging` NuGet package (v1.0.4) — same class/method surface, only the namespace changed. This is a **deployment-environment dependency, not a code limitation**: the target machine must have the Windows "Message Queuing" (MSMQ) feature installed, since the queue is still a local MSMQ queue under the hood. Confirmed present/running on the dev machine via `Get-Service -Name MSMQ`, but this must be flagged as a deployment prerequisite for other environments (containers/Linux hosts would not support this at all).
- **System.Web Adapters limitation** (`tasks/03.10-courses-controller-migration/progress-details.md`): `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SystemWebAdapters` is referenced/wired in `Program.cs`, but its shim only covers `HttpContext`/`Session`-style surface — not `System.Web.Mvc` controller/model-binding types. The one file upload case (`CoursesController` `HttpPostedFileBase` params) was converted directly to native `IFormFile` rather than routed through the adapters bridge, consistent with every other controller in the repo being fully rewritten to native ASP.NET Core MVC rather than leaning on the adapters shim for MVC surface.
- **Remaining literal "System.Web" text** (repo-wide grep, this task): zero hits in any `.cs` file. Two **legacy config files** still contain `System.Web.Mvc`/`System.Web.Optimization`/`System.Web.WebPages` strings: `Web.config` (`<system.web>` compilation/httpRuntime block plus the 14 leftover `<assemblyBinding>` entries above) and `Views/Web.config` (a classic ASP.NET Razor-view-engine config file — `system.web.webPages.razor`, `pageBaseType`, Razor host factory, etc.). Both are **inert under ASP.NET Core net10.0** (the hosting model doesn't read `system.web.webPages.razor` or classic Razor host-factory config at all), but `Web.config`'s `<connectionStrings>`/`<appSettings>` sections are still load-bearing — they're read via the `legacy.config` copy (`CopyLegacyConfigForConfigurationManager` MSBuild target) by `SchoolContextFactory` and `NotificationService`. Recommend as deferred cleanup: delete `Views/Web.config` entirely (unused under net10.0) and trim `Web.config` down to just `<connectionStrings>`/`<appSettings>` (drop `<system.web>` and `<runtime><assemblyBinding>`) — not done in this task since it's a passive verification gate, not a code-change task, and the scenario's binding-redirect strategy is document-first.
